Recommendation:
THAT Staff Report IN2026-07
, Municipal Engineering and Development Standards Update, be received;
AND THAT
Council approves and accepts the revisions to the Town of Collingwood Municipal Engineering Standards;
AND THAT
Council delegates authority to the Director of Infrastructure to consider and implement future administrative, technical, legislative, and housekeeping updates to the Municipal Engineering and Development Standards, including changes required to maintain consistency with applicable legislation, regulations, industry standards, and internal administrative practices, provided such updates do not materially alter the intent of the Standards, significantly impact development costs, levels of service, or public expectations, or introduce new policy directions; and that any substantive amendments be brought forward to Council for consideration and approval.

Recommendation:
WHEREAS
Council supports a sustainable community and investment-ready economy enabled by protecting and preserving Employment Areas to:
provide opportunities for a diversified economic base, including maintaining a range and choice of suitable sites for Employment Area uses which support a wide range of economic activities and ancillary uses, and takes into account the needs of existing and future businesses;
retain strategic sites for investment, including market-ready sites, and seeking to address potential barriers to investment; and
plan for accommodating Employment Area uses over the long-term that, by the nature of the uses, are best suited to locate in Employment Areas including but not limited to manufacturing, research and development in connection with manufacturing, warehousing and goods movement, and associated retail and office uses and ancillary facilities;
AND WHEREAS
Council further recognizes that the current economic realities of tariffs, rising costs, and the need to bolster the sustainability of local, regional and provincial supply chains, renders the protection of Employment Areas in alignment with Provincial direction increasingly paramount, particularly given the current forecasted long-term deficit of Employment Area land and the indirect impacts of attracting and retaining a diverse and skilled labour force in living-wage sectors;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THA
T Staff Report P2026-28, Municipally Initiated Industrial Zone Modifications Zoning By-law Amendment (Town-Wide), be received;
AND THAT
Council enact and pass the Zoning By-law Amendment, attached as Appendix A to this report.
